items.name: animated-price
items.title: Animated price
items.description: Currency-aware price transitions with the same soft count and blur across every price update.
items.docs: Data in, callbacks out. Locale defaults to en-US; pass your application locale explicitly. Reduced motion shows the final state immediately.

items.name: animated-price-demo
items.title: Animated price demo
items.description: An interactive example with real state changes and accessible controls.

items.name: product-card
items.title: Product card
items.description: A production product card for React and Next.js: image with hover zoom, sale and stock badges, compare-at price, colour swatches with radiogroup semantics, add to cart, and a matching skeleton.
items.docs: Pass a plain product object and handle onAddToCart; the card never fetches. Format prices before you pass them so the card stays locale-neutral. Use renderImage to plug in next/image.

items.name: product-card-demo
items.title: Product card demo
items.description: Two product cards: one on sale with colour variants, one sold out.

items.name: money
items.title: Money
items.description: Money in minor units with its currency, and the helpers every commerce item shares: format for a locale, sum and multiply without drift.

items.name: pay-button
items.title: Pay button
items.description: The checkout button with its whole life: the amount on it, locked until the form is valid, processing, the bank step, paid, and failed with a safe retry.
items.docs: Send every press's attempt id to your server as the idempotency key. Pass disabledReason while the form is invalid, status from your payment provider (or let the promise from onPay drive it), and call step.authenticating() when the bank asks for a confirmation. Inside a checkout form use type="submit".

items.name: pay-button-demo
items.title: Pay button demo
items.description: A working preview of Pay button.

items.name: product-tile
items.title: Product tile
items.description: A quiet product tile for editorial grids: one link, a picture that swaps on hover, the name and the price, with a skeleton and no buttons.
items.docs: Prices are minor units with a currency, and locale should always be passed so the price matches on the server and in the browser. The tile holds no button, so it is safe in a carousel; set priority on the first row and pass renderImage to use next/image. ProductTileSkeleton keeps the grid steady while data loads.

items.name: product-tile-demo
items.title: Product tile demo
items.description: A working preview of Product tile.

items.name: product-row-card
items.title: Product row card
items.description: A list-view product card for search results: picture, title, rating and facts, then the price block, stock in words and the actions.
items.docs: Prices are Money in minor units. The title is the stretched link; Add to cart and your wishlist control stay separate controls above it. onAddToCart may return a promise to show the busy state, and ProductRowCardSkeleton stands in while a list loads. On a phone the price block stacks above a full-width Add to cart that is 40px high, so give a wishlist control the same height.

items.name: product-row-card-demo
items.title: Product row card demo
items.description: A working preview of Product row card.

items.name: mini-product-row
items.title: Mini product row
items.description: A one-line product reference for suggestions, bundles and pickers: thumbnail, name, option and price, as a link, a button or a plain row.
items.docs: Give it href for a link or onClick for a button; with neither it is a plain row. trailing stays a separate control above the stretched link, so a checkbox or a remove button is safe. selected adds a check and aria-pressed (button) or aria-current (link).

items.name: mini-product-row-demo
items.title: Mini product row demo
items.description: A working preview of Mini product row.

items.name: base-price
items.title: Base price
items.description: The required price per 100 g or per litre, worked out from the pack size and price, converted, rounded half up and formatted for the locale.
items.docs: Pass the price of the pack in minor units, how much one pack holds and its unit; the base price is worked out here, rounded half up to the cent. Give it an id and point the price's aria-describedby at it. computeBasePrice is exported for sorting or analytics.

items.name: base-price-demo
items.title: Base price demo
items.description: A working preview of Base price.

items.name: price-range
items.title: Price range
items.description: A price for products with variants: 'From 19', '19 to 39' or one price, with sale ranges handled and struck through.
items.docs: min and max are minor units. variant="from" shows the lowest price after a word; variant="range" shows both ends with Intl formatRange. cents="auto" drops .00 when every figure is whole. The compare-at range is struck through only when it is higher.

items.name: price-range-demo
items.title: Price range demo
items.description: A working preview of Price range.

items.name: quantity-stepper
items.title: Quantity stepper
items.description: A quantity control for carts: minus, plus and a typed value, with pack steps, a stock cap, hold to repeat and remove at one.
items.docs: Controlled (value, onChange) or uncontrolled (defaultValue). min defaults to 1 and every value is min plus whole steps. stockLimit and max cap it; removeAtMin turns the minus into a trash button that calls onRemove. A press steps when it is released, so a scroll that starts on a button changes nothing; holding repeats, and neither a hold nor a key repeat ever removes the line. busy ignores presses and covers the number with a spinner without changing the size.

items.name: quantity-stepper-demo
items.title: Quantity stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Quantity stepper.

items.name: add-to-cart-button
items.title: Add to cart button
items.description: The buy button with its commerce states: select an option, adding, added with View cart, failed with retry, sold out and pre-order.
items.docs: onAdd may return a promise: the button is busy until it settles, says Added beside a View cart link, or shows an inline error that retries. Pass missingOption while a variant is unchosen, soldOut with onNotify for Notify me, preorder for a ship date, or drive it with status.

items.name: add-to-cart-button-demo
items.title: Add to cart button demo
items.description: A working preview of Add to cart button.

items.name: product-info-tabs
items.title: Product info tabs
items.description: Description, details, shipping and reviews as tabs on desktop and an accordion on a phone, from the same content.
items.docs: Give every section a short id: the URL hash #id opens it, and the hash follows the open section. Closed panels stay in the document. Below the breakpoint (768 px by default) the sections become a single-open accordion whose headings use headingLevel. The server renders the tabs, so until the page is interactive a small inline style hides the tab row under the breakpoint and a phone never paints a row that does not fit (a strict style-src policy blocks that rule; the row then scrolls inside itself).

items.name: product-info-tabs-demo
items.title: Product info tabs demo
items.description: A working preview of Product info tabs.

items.name: fit-scale
items.title: Fit scale
items.description: Where an item runs, from small to large, as a five-point scale with the marker placed from review data.
items.docs: value is the average fit from 1 (runs small) to 5 (runs large). Without a value, or with a count of 0, it renders nothing. Pass labels for another language: the sentence uses {fit} and {count}.

items.name: fit-scale-demo
items.title: Fit scale demo
items.description: A working preview of Fit scale.

items.name: shipping-estimator
items.title: Shipping estimator
items.description: Country and postcode in, delivery options out: the cart's shipping estimator with prices, arrival windows and a postcode check per country.
items.docs: onEstimate gets a country and a postcode that already match the country's format, and returns the options: an empty list means you do not ship there, a rejection shows a retry message. Amounts are in minor units. Pass onSelect and the list becomes a radio group; it is called with null when the choice no longer stands (the country or postcode was edited, or a new estimate started), so clear whatever you stored. Pass defaultOptions to restore an earlier estimate. postcodes.ts exports the format rules, so the same check can run on your server.

items.name: shipping-estimator-demo
items.title: Shipping estimator demo
items.description: A working preview of Shipping estimator.

items.name: order-line
items.title: Order line
items.description: A read-only order line: picture, name, option, quantity times unit price, line total and a per-line status, read out as one sentence.
items.docs: Amounts are in minor units. compareAtAmount draws a struck price, discount adds a line and takes its amount off the total. Put lines in a <ul>; use as="div" outside a list. Pass statusLabel to translate the chip.

items.name: order-line-demo
items.title: Order line demo
items.description: A working preview of Order line.

items.name: order-card
items.title: Order card
items.description: An order in a customer's history: number, date, status, thumbnails, total and the next step as a button, with the whole card linking to the order.
items.docs: Dates are ISO strings, read in timeZone (UTC by default) and written out in locale. The action that fits the status is chosen for you (track, reorder); give order.actions to choose your own (up to three; the first is the main button, and on a compact card they wrap to a second line when the row is narrow). The buttons sit above a stretched link. Give an action an address with actionHrefs and it is a link that needs no JavaScript; for the others pass onAction from a client component.

items.name: order-card-demo
items.title: Order card demo
items.description: A working preview of Order card.

items.name: order-lookup
items.title: Order lookup
items.description: Where is my order? An order number and email form for guests, with answers that never reveal who has orders.
items.docs: onLookup resolves with whatever should appear under the form, or with null when nothing matches: a missing order and a wrong email give the same words. Reject for a failure on your side. The answer under the form goes away as soon as a field is edited. Rate-limit the endpoint behind it; the form cannot do that for you.

items.name: order-lookup-demo
items.title: Order lookup demo
items.description: A working preview of Order lookup.

items.name: modifier-group
items.title: Modifier group
items.description: Options with rules for products and menus: required, pick one or up to N, price add-ons and a polite count of what is chosen.
items.docs: max 1 (the default) draws radios, anything more draws checkboxes that lock at the maximum; pass Infinity for no limit. min of 1 or more marks the group Required. Prices are in minor units. The message for a missing choice shows after the first change, or at once with invalid.

items.name: modifier-group-demo
items.title: Modifier group demo
items.description: A working preview of Modifier group.

items.name: view-cart-bar
items.title: View cart bar
items.description: A bar pinned to the bottom with item count, total and a View cart button, rising when the first item is added and resting above the footer.
items.docs: It is sticky, not fixed: render it as the last child of your page's main content, and it stays on the bottom edge of the screen while you scroll, then rests above the footer. total is in minor units. Use hidden on the cart page itself.

items.name: view-cart-bar-demo
items.title: View cart bar demo
items.description: A working preview of View cart bar.

items.name: promo-tile
items.title: Promo tile
items.description: A promotional tile for a product grid: a picture, a short headline and one action, one or two columns wide, with words on a solid plate.
items.docs: Put it in a grid next to product cards and add grid-flow-dense to the grid, so a wide tile never leaves a gap. span={2} applies from the sm breakpoint up; on a phone every tile is one column, and it fits its own track whether the grid has one column there or two. The picture is decorative unless you give it alt text, and a screen reader hears "Promotion" first.

items.name: promo-tile-demo
items.title: Promo tile demo
items.description: A working preview of Promo tile.

items.name: cart-issues
items.title: Cart issues
items.description: The problems in a cart that need fixing before checkout: unavailable lines, price changes and minimums, each with its one fix.
items.docs: Remove an issue from the list when you have fixed it or the shopper has dismissed it, and keep the component mounted when the list is empty: focus moves to the next action, or to the status line when the last one is gone. Everything blocks except a price change, unless you set blocking. Point your checkout button's aria-describedby at the region's id, or print summarizeCartIssues(issues).reason (from cart-issues/issues, which also runs on the server) next to it. onBlockingChange reports the change.

items.name: cart-issues-demo
items.title: Cart issues demo
items.description: A working preview of Cart issues.

items.name: rating-inline
items.title: Rating inline
items.description: Stars drawn to the exact average, the score and the review count in one line, linking to the reviews, for product titles and cards.
items.docs: Give it the average and the count; a count of zero shows emptyText ("No reviews yet"), or nothing with emptyText={null}. With href the whole line is a link. Pass label to translate the sentence a screen reader hears. To collect a rating use the Rating primitive.

items.name: rating-inline-demo
items.title: Rating inline demo
items.description: A working preview of Rating inline.

items.name: add-stepper
items.title: Add stepper
items.description: An Add button that turns into minus, count and plus in the same footprint once something is in the cart, as in ordering apps.
items.docs: Controlled with value and onChange, or uncontrolled with defaultValue; zero means not in the cart. stockLimit and max disable plus and print the reason under the control, without taking room, so leave a line of space there; busy keeps the width and the focus while your cart updates. Minus at min removes the item. Always pass label: it is in every accessible name.

items.name: add-stepper-demo
items.title: Add stepper demo
items.description: A working preview of Add stepper.

items.name: sales-unit-picker
items.title: Sales unit picker
items.description: Let shoppers buy by the piece, the box, the pallet or by weight: every unit shows its price per piece, switching converts the quantity, and the total is worked out.
items.docs: Describe the product's units with pieces (how many pieces one holds) and price in minor units; the price per piece, the saving against the smallest pack and the conversion between units all come from those two numbers. A unit's min, step and max are its rules: quantities are multiples of step, at least min, at most max, and a typed number is corrected with a message. Switching unit works from the pieces the shopper asked for and rounds up, never down, so looking at the units never changes the order: switch back and the same quantity returns. Typing, stepping or pushing against a limit is what changes the ask. onChange always carries a quantity the rules allow plus the line total. With mode="weight" pass pricePerKilo and the amounts are grams. units.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: sales-unit-picker-demo
items.title: Sales unit picker demo
items.description: A working preview of Sales unit picker.

items.name: quantity-calculator
items.title: Quantity calculator
items.description: Tell shoppers how many packs a job needs: enter an area or a length and width and a waste margin, and get whole packs rounded up, what they cover and the price.
items.docs: coveragePerPack is what one pack covers in unit (m2 or ft2); packPrice is in minor units and optional. The shopper types an area or a length and a width, and a waste margin that starts at wastePercent; a blank margin counts as wastePercent, as its placeholder says. Results always round up, and the panel says so. Typing 7,5 or 7.5 means the same, and 1,200 is read the way locale writes it. Every field has a message for a missing, unreadable, zero or too large number; maxArea is the largest believable area. onAddToCart receives the packs: return a promise and the button shows it is working, reject and the shopper is told. calculate.ts holds the arithmetic, counted in whole thousandths, and runs on the server too.

items.name: quantity-calculator-demo
items.title: Quantity calculator demo
items.description: A working preview of Quantity calculator.

items.name: compatibility-check
items.title: Compatibility check
items.description: Answer "will it fit?" for cases, filters and spare parts: pick a brand and a model and get compatible, not compatible with alternatives, or unknown, never a guess.
items.docs: Give it brands, models (each with the id of its brand) and the ids the product fits in compatible. Pass incompatible too when you know which models it does not fit: a model on neither list is then reported as unknown, instead of being guessed at. alternatives (by model id) are listed under a not-compatible answer, and contactHref adds an ask-us link to the unknown one. onCheck receives the brand, the model and the verdict whenever both are chosen: store that and pass it back as defaultValue to remember the last choice. productName is the subject of a sentence ("Halcyon MagGrip car mount fits the Orbit One."), so keep it singular or change the wording with labels. Until a brand is chosen the model field is disabled, and a line of text under it says why. fit.ts holds verdictFor and runs on the server too.

items.name: compatibility-check-demo
items.title: Compatibility check demo
items.description: A working preview of Compatibility check.

items.name: shoppable-list
items.title: Shoppable list
items.description: A recipe or project as a shopping list: amounts that scale with servings, substitutes for sold-out lines, and one button that adds the checked products to the cart.
items.docs: Each item is a product (id, name, price of one pack, optional packSize) with the amount the recipe needs for servings people. With servings the list gets a servings field and every amount scales, and so does the number of packs: 600 g needs two 500 g packs. A line with no amount (note: "to taste") is bought once. defaultChecked: false starts a line unchecked, for things the reader probably owns. A sold-out line (inStock: false) cannot be checked and offers its substitute; swapping checks it and onAddAll then carries the substitute's id. onAddAll receives only the checked lines, each with the product id, the packs, the price of one pack and the total; return a promise and the button shows it is working. list.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: shoppable-list-demo
items.title: Shoppable list demo
items.description: A working preview of Shoppable list.

items.name: round-up-toggle
items.title: Round up toggle
items.description: Offer to round the order up to the next euro for a good cause: the exact extra amount and the cause are in the question, and the switch starts off.
items.docs: total and step are in minor units: 2457 with a step of 100 offers to round up by 43 to 2500. It is off until the shopper turns it on, so it never nudges; defaultChecked is for restoring their own earlier choice. onChange receives the new state and { amount, total }: add amount to the order as a donation while it is on. When the total is already a multiple of the step the component renders nothing, so treat the donation as zero. cause is in the question, always. round-up.ts holds roundUpOf, which runs on the server too, so the order you charge is computed the same way you showed it.

items.name: round-up-toggle-demo
items.title: Round up toggle demo
items.description: A working preview of Round up toggle.

items.name: installment-line
items.title: Installment line
items.description: The "or pay in 3 × 33.00" line under a price, with a popover for the schedule and terms: parts that add up exactly, fees stated, no provider logo.
items.docs: price and fee are in minor units. The parts are worked out so they always add up to price plus fee: what does not divide evenly goes on the first payment, and the line says so ("the first 37.52"). interval is week, two-weeks or month. Without now the details say how long after the first each payment is taken, which is the same on the server and in the browser; pass now (and timeZone) to give every payment its date. minPrice and maxPrice are the range you allow: outside it nothing is rendered. A fee of 0 says there is no fee; leave fee out to say nothing. terms is the small print. It has no state of its own, so it renders in a Server Component. installments.ts holds planInstallments and paymentDays, which run on the server too, so the schedule you charge is the one you showed.

items.name: installment-line-demo
items.title: Installment line demo
items.description: A working preview of Installment line.

items.name: return-window
items.title: Return window
items.description: Show how long an order can still be returned: the closing date, the days left, and open, closing soon and closed states, with Start return only while it is open.
items.docs: deliveredAt is an ISO date-time or a plain date such as "2026-10-20"; windowDays is how many days after the delivery day returns are accepted, so delivered 2 October with 30 days the last day is 1 November. Whole calendar days are counted in timeZone, which should be the shop's: the window closes at midnight there. Under soonDays (3) days left it is closing soon; on the last day it says so; the day after it is closed and the button goes. Pass now from the server for a first render that matches the browser; without it the first render shows only the date and the days appear once the browser's clock is read, so a cached page never claims days it cannot know. Start return is a button with onStartReturn, or a link with startReturnHref. window.ts holds the calendar arithmetic and runs on the server too, so you can refuse a late return there with the same rule.

items.name: return-window-demo
items.title: Return window demo
items.description: A working preview of Return window.

items.name: order-edit-window
items.title: Order edit window
items.description: Tell shoppers a fresh order can still be changed: the time left in words, actions to edit the address or items or cancel, and a calm swap when time is up.
items.docs: editableUntil is the moment the order stops being editable, with its offset ("2026-10-20T10:24:00Z"). The time is written in whole minutes, rounded down, and updates once a minute; only the 10 minute and 1 minute marks and the end are announced, politely, and never for where the time already stands when the page loads. At zero both sentences are laid in one cell, so the strip does not change size, the actions go aria-disabled (still focusable, so a keyboard user is not dropped), and onExpire is called once; never trust the browser for this, lock the order on your server as well. onAction receives address, items or cancel; cancel is only reported after the shopper confirms in the dialog, whose focus starts on Keep order. windowMinutes (optional) is the length of the whole window and adds a thin bar for how much is left. Pass now in tests and previews; without it the first render says "You can still change this order" and the time appears once the browser's clock is read. remaining.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: order-edit-window-demo
items.title: Order edit window demo
items.description: A working preview of Order edit window.

items.name: courier-card
items.title: Courier card
items.description: The delivery driver at a glance: photo or initial, first name, vehicle and plate, rating and arrival time, with Call and Message buttons and a same-size waiting state.
items.docs: Pass the courier (a first name, and optionally photo, vehicle, plate, rating) and eta in minutes; send a new eta whenever your tracking has one. The card shows only the first word of the name and never draws a phone number: onCall and onMessage are buttons you handle, or callHref and messageHref make them links, in which case use a relay or masked number, since the href is in the page. Both are named for the courier ("Call Mehmet"). The visible arrival time follows every update; the spoken one waits for it to settle and only speaks when the state changes, the time moved by two minutes or more, or the courier is about to arrive. Without a courier (or with status="pending") the card keeps its size and says "Looking for a courier"; the buttons are there but disabled. status="arrived" ends the countdown. eta.ts holds firstName and the rule for what is worth saying, and runs on the server too.

items.name: courier-card-demo
items.title: Courier card demo
items.description: A working preview of Courier card.

items.name: kitchen-ticket
items.title: Kitchen ticket
items.description: A kitchen order ticket: number, order type, items with modifiers, an elapsed timer that escalates in words, allergies read first and a Bump button.
items.docs: Pass one clock as now to every ticket on the board (a number, a date or an ISO string), so they tick together and render the same on the server. thresholds sets in minutes when a ticket runs slow (default 8) and when it is late (default 12). Without status the ticket keeps its own open or bumped state; pass status and handle onBump and onRecall to control it from your list, and take the ticket off the screen yourself. Allergies are set apart in an inverted block and come first in the reading order. A bumped ticket stops its timer at order.bumpedAt, or at the moment of the bump. labels holds every word, for another language.

items.name: kitchen-ticket-demo
items.title: Kitchen ticket demo
items.description: A working preview of Kitchen ticket.

items.name: bank-transfer-details
items.title: Bank transfer details
items.description: How to pay by bank transfer: beneficiary, IBAN, BIC, the exact amount and the reference, each with a copy button, and the deadline.
items.docs: details (a BankTransferAccount) holds the account: beneficiary, iban, an optional bic, amount in minor units and the reference. The IBAN is shown in groups of four and copied without spaces, the amount is copied without a symbol and with the decimal mark of locale, and the reference is copied exactly as given. onCopy receives the row ("iban") and the text that reached the clipboard. deadline is when the order lapses, written in timeZone; pass now from the server and a deadline that has passed turns the buttons off and says so at the top of the card, in place of the instructions. Without now nothing is ever shown as lapsed. In a card narrower than 26rem the copy buttons are only their icon (still named Copy IBAN), so an account number keeps one line. labels holds every word, for another language.

items.name: bank-transfer-details-demo
items.title: Bank transfer details demo
items.description: A working preview of Bank transfer details.

items.name: seller-card
items.title: Seller card
items.description: Who sells this: name, verification in words, rating, items sold, reply time and member since, with Contact and Visit store as separate actions.
items.docs: Pass the seller as data: name, an optional logo (initials are drawn without one), verified, rating with reviews, itemsSold, replyMinutes and memberSince as an ISO date. What is missing is left out; a seller with no sales and no reviews shows New seller, and a rating is only shown with a review count above zero. The rating is the inline rating, so it says the same sentence to a screen reader. Contact is a button (onContact) or, with contactHref, a link; Visit store appears when you pass storeHref. The figures sit in a row once the card is wide enough and in a list when it is not, whatever the screen. compact is the smaller card for beside the price; a long name wraps to two lines and is in the title of the heading. Always pass locale so the numbers and the date match on the server and in the browser; a bare memberSince date is a calendar day and ignores timeZone. labels holds every word.

items.name: seller-card-demo
items.title: Seller card demo
items.description: A working preview of Seller card.

items.name: care-instructions
items.title: Care instructions
items.description: Garment care as a row of drawn symbols, each with its meaning in words: wash, bleach, tumble dry, dry, iron and professional care.
items.docs: care is an object of settings: wash ("95", "60", "50", "40", "30", "hand", "no"), bleach, tumbleDry, dry, iron and dryClean. Leave one out, or pass a value that is not known, and it is skipped, never drawn as something close; with nothing to show it renders nothing. layout="row" puts the words under each symbol, layout="list" beside it. showLabels={false} gives a row of bare symbols that are focusable and say their instruction in a tooltip and to a screen reader. labels replaces the words by key, for example { "wash-30": "Wasmachine, max 30 degrees" }.

items.name: care-instructions-demo
items.title: Care instructions demo
items.description: A working preview of Care instructions.

items.name: grade-scale
items.title: Grade scale
items.description: A letter-grade scale such as an energy class or eco score: the whole range drawn, steps that differ in length, the product's grade enlarged.
items.docs: grades runs from the best grade to the worst, so the first step is the shortest bar and the last the longest. value must be one of them: anything else draws the scale without a marker and the sentence says the product is not graded. label names what is graded and starts the sentence a screen reader hears. It draws a scale, not an official label: bring certified data to it.

items.name: grade-scale-demo
items.title: Grade scale demo
items.description: A working preview of Grade scale.

items.name: order-matrix
items.title: Order matrix
items.description: Order a product by size and colour in one grid: a quantity field per cell, stock hints, row and column totals, and paste from a spreadsheet.
items.docs: rows are the variants (colours or widths, with an optional swatch) and columns the sizes. stock holds what can be ordered per row id and column id: a cell that is missing is not made in that size and is disabled (a dash), zero is sold out and says Sold out under the field, and a quantity is held to its stock and said so; with lowStockAt or fewer left a cell says how many. Control the quantities with value and onChange or leave them to defaultValue; a cell at zero is left out of the object. minPerCell flags a quantity above zero but below the minimum and keeps Add from being pressed. unitPrice (minor units) adds the money. onAddAll receives every line and the totals and may return a promise. Arrow keys and Enter move between cells, and pasting a block of numbers from a spreadsheet fills the grid from the cell you are in. A grid wider than its frame scrolls sideways, keeps its first column in view (the field the keyboard moves to is scrolled clear of that column) and says so under the grid. Every field is named Navy, size M; labels holds every word, including the name pattern. Always pass locale.

items.name: order-matrix-demo
items.title: Order matrix demo
items.description: A working preview of Order matrix.

items.name: shipment-group
items.title: Shipment group
items.description: Items grouped by shipment: where it ships from, the delivery method and window, a status, then the lines that travel in that parcel.
items.docs: Pass the shipment (where it ships from, the delivery method with its price in minor units and an arrival window as ISO dates, and kind and shipsOn for a pre-order or a backorder), index and total, a status and the lines as children. Give each line its own vertical padding: the group draws the rules between them. With total of 1 the heading is dropped and only the delivery and the lines remain. status writes a badge that follows the shipment from Not shipped yet to Delivered, Delayed or Cancelled, and the card follows it: a delivered shipment says Arrived (pass the day it came as method.from), a cancelled one says nothing is on its way and mutes its price and lines, and a pre-order or backorder only says when it ships until it has left. Change is a button (onChangeMethod) or, with changeHref, a link, and it is only offered while the method can still change: not once the shipment is shipped, out for delivery, delivered or cancelled. Pass canChange to decide yourself. The group is a labelled region named by its heading. Always pass locale; a bare ISO date is a calendar day and ignores timeZone. labels holds every word.

items.name: shipment-group-demo
items.title: Shipment group demo
items.description: A working preview of Shipment group.

items.name: dimension-diagram
items.title: Dimension diagram
items.description: Product dimensions drawn as a simple box, cylinder or flat shape with width, height and depth labelled, switchable between cm and inches.
items.docs: width, height and depth are in unit (centimetres by default); a cylinder takes its diameter as width, and without a depth the drawing is a flat elevation. The drawing scales to its container and the labels keep their size; when the drawing is small or the product narrow, the width label drops just below its line so the arrows stay in sight, and a label on the object gives up its name and keeps its figure (the names are always in the text above the drawing). A switch converts between the units in units and rounds the way a shop writes it (80 cm is 31.5 in); keep the choice yourself with displayUnit and onDisplayUnitChange so one switch can drive every diagram on the page, or leave it to defaultDisplayUnit. extras adds measurements such as { label: "Seat height", value: 46 } as a dashed line across the drawing. The same numbers are written above the drawing and as one sentence for a screen reader. Always pass locale.

items.name: dimension-diagram-demo
items.title: Dimension diagram demo
items.description: A working preview of Dimension diagram.

items.name: refund-tracker
items.title: Refund tracker
items.description: Where a refund is: requested, received, approved and paid out, with dates, the amount and the expected arrival once it is approved.
items.docs: refund holds the amount in minor units, where it goes, and steps: an ISO date for each step that has happened (requested, received, approved, paid). The latest step with a date is the current one; steps before it count as done. expectedBy is shown only once the refund is approved, and without it the item says Usually 3 to 5 working days after approval. Pass now from the server and a date that has passed is called late. refund.issue explains a failed refund (it stops at its step and shows reason and action) or a partial one (refunded is the amount that is paid). Always pass locale; labels holds every word, for another language.

items.name: refund-tracker-demo
items.title: Refund tracker demo
items.description: A working preview of Refund tracker.

items.name: bill-splitter
items.title: Bill splitter
items.description: Split the bill at the table: equally or by item, with a tip and an optional round-up, in whole cents so the shares always add up to the bill.
items.docs: Pass the bill as total in minor units (9640 is 96.40) and people as a count or as names. With items (name, amount and sharedBy, the positions of the people who had it) the bill can also be split by item: a line with no names is shared by everyone, and whatever the lines do not cover (a service charge, a discount) is shared in proportion to what each person had and shown as its own row. tipPercent starts the tip and tipOptions sets the choices. The count of people, the sharedBy of each line and tipPercent are starting values: after that the people at the table change them on the screen, and a later change of the prop does not undo that (give the component a new key to start over). Every sum is done in whole minor units and the odd cent goes to the first people in line, so the shares always add up to the bill; in an equal split the screen names who pays the cent more. defaultRoundUp lifts every share to a whole unit and shows the difference as its own line. onPay receives each share (subtotal, tip, rounding and total) when its button is pressed: return a promise to show it is working, reject to keep the share unpaid and say so. Once someone has paid, the split is fixed. Pass paid (positions) to control who has paid. Without onPay the splitter is a calculator with no buttons. Someone without a name is Guest 1, Guest 2 and so on (labels.guest). The chips under a dish and the sentence about the odd cent use short names: the first name, the first name with the initial of the last name ('Anna V.') when two first names collide, and a guest's whole label, so two chips never read the same. In a wide card up to four people sit beside the dish on one line; with more they stay under it and wrap. The result is a polite status; labels holds every word.

items.name: bill-splitter-demo
items.title: Bill splitter demo
items.description: A working preview of Bill splitter.

items.name: rental-rates
items.title: Rental rates
items.description: Rental pricing by period: day, weekend, week and month rates, the cheapest mix for the dates picked, and the refundable deposit apart.
items.docs: Pass rates as the price of one whole period in minor units: { day: 3500, weekend: 9000, week: 18000, month: 52000 }; leave out what you do not offer. A weekend is Friday to Sunday (Saturday and Sunday count too), a week is 7 days and a month is 30. The cheapest combination for the days picked is worked out exactly (it may buy a week for six days, or a week and three days), and the breakdown names every line, with what it saves against the day rate in a sentence such as '3 days at the weekend rate saves €15.00'. Every rate shows what one day costs on it. range and onRangeChange control the dates (Dates at midnight, like the house date pickers; range also takes a plain '2026-11-20' string), or leave them out and pass defaultRange. unavailable lists the booked days as Dates or strings: they are struck through, cannot be picked, and while the return day is chosen the days after the next booking are refused too; the booked days of the month are named under the calendar. min is the first day that can be rented. Choosing a rate fills in the dates for one whole period from the pick-up day, or from today, moving to the next stretch where it is free and saying so under the chosen dates in the summary, so the calendar stays where it is. deposit is shown apart from the total and described as refundable. The total is a polite status. labels holds every word; pricing.ts holds the arithmetic and runs on the server too.

items.name: rental-rates-demo
items.title: Rental rates demo
items.description: A working preview of Rental rates.

items.name: shelf-label
items.title: Shelf label
items.description: A retail shelf label: name, big price with raised cents, unit price and a scannable barcode, in black on white and printable at true size.
items.docs: Pass product, price in minor units, a barcode and, for goods sold by weight or volume, unitPrice as { amount, per }: '€2.49 per kg'. The barcode is an EAN-13, a UPC-A (12 digits) or an EAN-8 with its check digit, drawn as SVG with the digits under the bars the way the standard sets them; a wrong check digit is not drawn as a code, the label says what the digit should be. promotion puts a black strip across the top; detail adds a second line under the name. size is small (50 × 30 mm), medium (60 × 40 mm) or large (100 × 60 mm): on screen a label is drawn at about its printed size (the small ones a little larger, so their text stays readable) and everything inside is measured against the label itself, so it scales as one. The barcode takes the room the text above it leaves: a two-line name with a detail under a promotion makes it a little smaller instead of running into it, and the promotion stays on one line and is cut short with an ellipsis. The label is always black on white so it scans reliably, in the dark theme too. Mark labels printable and a print stylesheet takes everything else off the paper: each label prints at its true size in millimetres with its bars and strip, flowing down the page; the stylesheet uses :has(), which every current browser supports. The price is read out in full and drawn with its cents set small and raised. ean.ts holds the barcode arithmetic and runs on the server too. labels holds the three fixed phrases.

items.name: shelf-label-demo
items.title: Shelf label demo
items.description: A working preview of Shelf label.

items.name: search-results-header
items.title: Search results header
items.description: The top of a shop search results page: the query as the h1, a polite count, a did-you-mean correction, category tabs with counts and related searches.
items.docs: Pass the query as typed and the total across all categories. The heading repeats what was searched with the number of results (headingAs is h1 by default; use h2 inside a page that has one). When the shop searched for something else, pass correctedQuery: the heading names that, and a line says 'Showing results for shirt. Search instead for shrit.' with two real links. categories are the tabs (id, label, count), the first being the unfiltered All; they are controlled with activeCategory and onCategoryChange, or keep themselves with defaultCategory. related are the chips under them and sort is a slot at the end of that row, for a sort menu; on a phone it gets a row of its own at full width, so give it something that can grow. Related searches and the correction are real links built with searchHref (default ?q=term); pass onSearch(term) to take a plain click yourself while modified clicks still open a new tab. The count is announced politely when it changes: the total, or the count of the chosen category. With total 0 the heading says 'No results for' and the tabs are hidden; render the empty-search state in the results area below. EmptySearch repeats the query in a title of its own, so when it sits under this heading you can keep that title for screen readers only, as the demo does. labels holds every word.

items.name: search-results-header-demo
items.title: Search results header demo
items.description: A working preview of Search results header.

items.name: checkout-sign-in-choice
items.title: Checkout sign-in choice
items.description: The fork before checkout: sign in, or continue as a guest with just an email, with what an account adds stated plainly.
items.docs: Two cards side by side, stacked on a phone with the guest card first; side by side they share their rows, so the headings and the first fields line up whatever the length of the descriptions. onSignIn receives { email, password } once both are filled in, and onContinueAsGuest receives the guest's email: return, or resolve to, a sentence when it fails ('That email and password do not match.') and it is shown in an announced alert in that card; return nothing when it worked. Each form checks itself when it is sent, writes the problem under the field and moves focus there. providers is a slot under the sign-in form after an 'or' rule, for a passkey or an email link. forgotHref shows the forgot link beside the password; createAccountHref (a link) or onCreateAccount (a button) is the way to an account, under a list of what an account adds (benefits, three read best). defaultEmail starts the sign-in with a known address. headingAs is h1 by default; the cards' titles sit one level below, and each card is a labelled region. labels holds every word.

items.name: checkout-sign-in-choice-demo
items.title: Checkout sign-in choice demo
items.description: A working preview of Checkout sign-in choice.

items.name: returns-policy-section
items.title: Returns policy section
items.description: Returns explained for humans: the window, how it works in four steps, what can and cannot be returned, and when the refund arrives.
items.docs: It works with no props: the copy it starts with is a real, shippable returns policy (30 days from delivery, four steps, what can and cannot be returned, refund times by payment method). Every line is a prop, so the legal wording can be swapped for each shop: windowDays fills the headline and the rule in words, facts are the terms beside the headline, steps (title, description, icon) are drawn as a numbered strip, eligible and excluded are one line each with a check or a cross, refundTimes are rows of the table (method, time, note), notice is a callout under it (a note unless you set its tone to tip or warning), startHref adds the Start a return button and contact a line with the way to reach someone. An empty facts, steps, eligible, excluded or refundTimes leaves that part out. headingAs is h2 by default; with h1 the titles of the parts are h2 and the steps h3. linkAs renders the links with your router's Link. It keeps no state, so it renders on the server. labels holds the fixed words.

items.name: returns-policy-section-demo
items.title: Returns policy section demo
items.description: A working preview of Returns policy section.

items.name: shipping-rates-table
items.title: Shipping rates table
items.description: Where you ship and what it costs: regions, methods, prices, delivery times and the free-shipping threshold in one table, with a country picker.
items.docs: zones lists the regions in the order they should appear: region, countries (they fill the country picker; without them it lists the regions) and methods with name, price in minor units (0 is shown as Free, and its free-from cell says Always free), days (a number, a [fastest, slowest] pair or your own sentence, always in working days) and freeFrom, the order amount from which that method is free; a paid method without one shows a dash, read out as No free option. On a phone the Free from row is left out for both. Choosing a country marks its region's rows Your region in words as well as a tint and brings them into view; highlight starts with a country or a region already marked. cutoff is the dispatch cut-off in a sentence and notes are callouts under the table (customs, holidays, cut-off times). On a phone every region is a card with its methods and a description list, so nothing scrolls sideways. currency and locale format the amounts. headingAs is h2 by default; with h1 the region cards on a phone are h2. labels holds every word.

items.name: shipping-rates-table-demo
items.title: Shipping rates table demo
items.description: A working preview of Shipping rates table.

items.name: customer-account-home
items.title: Customer account home
items.description: The landing of 'My account': a greeting, the latest order with its status, and quick links with counts to orders, addresses, returns and help.
items.docs: Pass the customer's name and memberSince as an ISO date (shown as the month and the year). latestOrder carries the number, status (processing, shipped, delivered or cancelled), placedAt, items for the thumbnails (three are drawn, the rest become +2, itemCount says how many there are in all), total in minor units and deliveryDate: the status is written out in words, and while the order is on its way with a trackHref a Track link appears. Without an order the card becomes No orders yet with a Start shopping link (shopHref), so a new account never meets a hole. links are the tiles under it: label, href, an optional count (zero is shown), a hint line and an icon; the tiles wrap and the last row stretches, so there is never an empty cell. nudge is a slot under the grid for a loyalty note or a verification reminder. linkAs renders the links with your router's Link; renderImage plugs in next/image. locale and timeZone format the dates. It keeps no state, so it renders on the server. labels holds every word.

items.name: customer-account-home-demo
items.title: Customer account home demo
items.description: A working preview of Customer account home.

items.name: order-help-options
items.title: Order help options
items.description: 'Need help with this order?': the actions that fit its status, each saying why it is available or, with the date, why it is not.
items.docs: Pass the order (number, status of processing, packed, shipped, delivered or cancelled, and deliveredAt and returnUntil as ISO dates) and the block works the list out itself: Track opens while it ships, Change address and Cancel close when the order is packed, Return opens at delivery and closes with the return window, and Report a problem is always there. An action that is not possible stays in the list, dimmed and marked aria-disabled, with its reason and the date in words: Tab still lands on it, so the reason is read out, and pressing it does nothing, and the status leads the block as a sentence so people see why the list looks as it does. Give the first available recommended action a solid button by setting primary on it. Pass your own actions (id, title, description, available, reason, href, label, primary, icon) when you have worked availability out on the server. onSelect receives the id of the pressed action; an action with an href is a link. contact adds the row at the end. Pass now (an ISO date-time) so the return window is judged against the same moment on the server and in the browser; without it the window counts as open until the browser's clock says otherwise. timeZone is the shop's: calendar days are counted there. labels holds every word, the reasons included.

items.name: order-help-options-demo
items.title: Order help options demo
items.description: A working preview of Order help options.

items.name: category-product-rows
items.title: Category product rows
items.description: Several categories on one page, each with its name, a View all link and a short row of product cards, so the whole catalogue reads at a glance.
items.docs: Pass categories: each has a name (the heading of its section), an href, an optional description line, total (how many products the category holds in all, the number in 'View all 48') and products in the ProductCard shape. perRow (2 to 6, default 4) says how many cards a row holds on a wide screen and so how many of the products are drawn; a phone always shows two across, and the grid answers to the width of the block itself rather than the screen, so it also works beside a sidebar. A category with fewer products than a row shows what it has, with no placeholders; one with none says so, and a category whose total is 0 has no link. Hairlines divide the sections and every section is a region named by its own heading. The 'View all' link is named for a screen reader as 'View all 48 in Kitchen knives', so six of them are not six of the same. onAddToCart and renderImage go to every card. linkAs renders the links with your router's Link, locale writes the totals and labels holds the fixed words. Apart from the cards it keeps no state, so it renders on the server.

items.name: category-product-rows-demo
items.title: Category product rows demo
items.description: A working preview of Category product rows.

items.name: reorder-list
items.title: Reorder list
items.description: Order again: the products a customer buys regularly, with the last order date, a quantity on every line and a button to add one line or all of them.
items.docs: Pass items: id, name, an optional variant, image and href, price in minor units (1850 is 18.50) with an optional per ('each', 'per case'), lastOrderedAt (an ISO date), lastQuantity (the quantity starts there, kept inside max) and unavailable, the reason in words for a product that cannot be bought now: its line stays in the list, switched off, with the reason where 'Last ordered' would be. Every line has a checkbox, a quantity and an Add button. onAdd(id, quantity) receives the quantity to add now (return a promise and the button shows it is working; reject and the line says so). The list remembers what it put in the bag, so the number on a line and the number in the bag never disagree: a line that is in the bag says Added with a check, raising its quantity makes the button say 'Add 2 more' and sends only those 2, and lowering it under what is in the bag switches the button off and says 'In bag: 4'. The footer adds up what is still to add in an animated price, and its button calls onAddAll(lines) with every ticked line that has something left to add, each line's quantity being that difference; without onAddAll it calls onAdd for each line. Once everything ticked is in the bag, the footer says what is in the bag. onRemove(id) is called by 'Not interested': the line gives way to 'Removed. Undo' for six seconds and then leaves, and Undo calls onUnremove(id) so you can take the saved choice back. Pass now from the server so 'Last ordered 3 weeks ago' matches in the browser; without it the dates are shown first and the browser's clock turns them into words once the page has loaded. currency, locale and timeZone format the prices and the calendar days. A polite status says what was added and, once ticking settles, what is selected. headingAs and labels do the usual.

items.name: reorder-list-demo
items.title: Reorder list demo
items.description: A working preview of Reorder list.

items.name: brand-index
items.title: Brand index
items.description: A shop-by-brand page: popular brands as tiles, every brand under its letter with a product count, a search field and an A to Z jump bar.
items.docs: Pass brands (name, href, an optional count and logo { src, alt }) in any order: they are sorted for the locale and grouped under their first letter, with accents folded (Élan sits under E) and names that start with a number or a symbol under #. popular is a list of brand names to draw as tiles above the list, in that order. A tile shows the logo as a one-colour silhouette in the text colour, so pass a transparent SVG or PNG, or the brand's initials when there is no logo. The A to Z bar fills the width, scrolls sideways on a phone (the next letter peeks in to say so, and a search scrolls it to the first letter that still has a brand), sticks to the top (or below the CSS variable --sticky-top, which you set to the height of your own sticky header) and shows the letters that have no brand without linking them. The search field filters as you type, ignoring case and accents; the bar follows the matches, a polite status says how many brands match, and an empty result offers to show all brands. Every group is an h3 that a screen reader hears as 'Brands starting with A', and the columns balance on a wide screen and become one on a phone. linkAs renders every link with your router's Link: the links are drawn on the server and handed to the searchable part, so it works from a Server Component, and without JavaScript the whole list is there. With no brands at all it says so, with no count above it. locale, title, description, headingAs and labels do the usual.

items.name: brand-index-demo
items.title: Brand index demo
items.description: A working preview of Brand index.

items.name: reviews-to-write
items.title: Reviews to write
items.description: Delivered products waiting for a review: a star pick per product that folds into a thank-you, with Write a review and a Skip that can be undone.
items.docs: Pass items: id, name, an optional variant, image, href and reviewHref, deliveredAt (an ISO date, written as '12 May' in locale and timeZone) and an optional rating when the customer already gave stars somewhere else, such as an order email: the row then starts as a thank-you. Picking a star calls onRate(id, rating). A click or a tap answers at once; with the keyboard the arrow keys move through the stars and Space or Enter gives the answer, as does moving focus away from them; only three seconds without a change give it for the person. The row folds into 'Thanks, you gave it 4 out of 5: Very good.' with an 'Add a few words' link, an anchor when the item has reviewHref and otherwise a button that calls onWrite(id, rating), and a 'Change' button that brings the stars back so a slip can be put right: the next answer calls onRate again. Return a promise from onRate: if it rejects, the row goes back to its stars and says so. Skip calls onSkip(id), closes the row and shows a toast with Undo, which calls onUnskip(id): mount the RHS UI Toaster once in your app. Focus follows the row that folds, leaves or comes back, a polite status says what happened, and when nothing is left an empty state says so kindly. ratingWords and every other word are in labels.

items.name: reviews-to-write-demo
items.title: Reviews to write demo
items.description: A working preview of Reviews to write.

items.name: pickup-ready-card
items.title: Pickup ready card
items.description: Your order is ready to collect: a large pickup code with copy and a QR slot, the shop, today's hours, what to bring and how long it is held.
items.docs: Pass order, code, store ({ name, address: string[], phone }), hours (today's opening hours in words), heldUntil, bring (a list; it defaults to a photo ID and the code), directionsHref and, for shops that scan, qr: a QR code from your own library, drawn in a white box so it reads in the dark theme too. heldUntil is a date such as '2026-10-30', which holds the order through the end of that day in timeZone, or a date-time, which holds it until then; it is written as a <time> element. Once it has passed the card says 'Pickup window ended', takes the code out of use, drops the copy button and the QR code and shows a contact line with the shop's number as a tel: link, and a polite status says so once. Pass now from the server for a first render that matches the browser's; without it the browser's clock is read after the page has loaded and again when the tab comes back or a minute passes. The code is plain selectable text and is read out one character at a time. The shop and the hours sit beside their words once the card is wide enough and under them in a narrow column. onCopy receives the code. locale, timeZone, headingAs and labels do the usual.

items.name: pickup-ready-card-demo
items.title: Pickup ready card demo
items.description: A working preview of Pickup ready card.

items.name: trade-account-application
items.title: Trade account application
items.description: A dealer or trade account request: company and VAT details, business type, expected spend and a reference, then what happens next.
items.docs: onSubmit(values) receives the company name, registration number, VAT number (cleaned, in capitals), country code, contact name, job title, email, phone, the businessType and monthlySpend values, the attached reference File or null and acceptedTerms. Return a string to say the shop could not take it: it is shown at the top and every answer stays. Return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by the confirmation. The checks run on send: company, registration and VAT numbers (two letters, then the number), country, name, email, a phone with at least six digits when one is given, the type, the spend and the terms. The problems are listed in a group at the top that takes focus and links to each field, and a field that shows one is checked again as it changes. businessTypes (value, title, description, icon) are the cards, spendBands (value, label) fill the select and countries is a list of ISO codes written in locale. The business types sit in one column until the form itself is wide enough for two cards, and every required answer is marked as required for assistive technology. termsHref makes the words 'trade terms' a link, reviewDays is the promise (default 2) and defaultValues prefills. submitted shows the confirmation for answers a page has already taken: what was given, what happens next (the steps are in labels) and a link to shopHref. It is not a <form> element, because Radix inputs inside one make React warn in development, but Enter in a text field still sends it. Every word is in labels.

items.name: trade-account-application-demo
items.title: Trade account application demo
items.description: A working preview of Trade account application.

items.name: delivery-instructions
items.title: Delivery instructions
items.description: Where the courier should leave it: hand over, door, neighbour or locker, with the safe choice first and only the fields that choice needs.
items.docs: A fieldset that is controlled with value and onChange or keeps its own state from defaultValue; the value is { dropOff, neighbour, code, phone, note, saveAsDefault }. options (value, title, description, icon, flag, fields) are the cards, safest first: description is the line about the risk the choice carries, flag is a short word such as 'Safest', and fields lists which of 'neighbour', 'code', 'phone' and 'note' that choice needs. Only those fields are shown, in place, and a polite status names the choice and the fields that appeared. The layout answers to the width of the fieldset, not of the screen: the cards sit one above the other until there is room for two, so it also works in a drawer or beside a sidebar on a wide screen. The code and the phone number share a row, and whichever of them is asked for alone takes the whole row. The access or gate code is masked with a button to show it, the note is a textarea with a counter against noteLimit (default 200) and showPhone={false} leaves out the phone number for the courier. Under 'Save as my default for future orders' a line says in words whether the instructions apply to this order only or to the next ones too. locale joins the list that is read out after a choice and labels holds every word.

items.name: delivery-instructions-demo
items.title: Delivery instructions demo
items.description: A working preview of Delivery instructions.

items.name: trade-credit-summary
items.title: Trade credit summary
items.description: A trade customer's credit at a glance: what is available, a meter that warns in words, payment terms, what is overdue and the next due date.
items.docs: Pass limit and used in minor units, terms in words ('30 days net'), nextDue ({ date, amount }) and overdue ({ amount, count, since }); account is a line under the heading. The big figure is what is available to spend and the meter shows what is used. It warns in words from warnAt (default 0.8) of the limit, 'You have used 91% of your credit. An order over €2,250.00 may wait until a payment clears.', and says so when nothing is left. The meter, the badge and the words read the same unrounded share, so they agree on where 'near' begins; the meter turns red from 95 percent, or from warnAt when that is higher. The badge reads Good standing, Near your limit, Limit reached, Payment overdue or On hold, always as words with a glyph. overdue gets its own line with the amount, how many invoices and the oldest due date, and a Pay now button when onPay is passed: return a promise and it shows it is working; reject and the line says the payment could not start. blocked ({ reason, contact }) puts a notice at the top, takes the figure to zero and says who to call. requestForm is a slot that opens under 'Request a higher limit' (defaultRequestOpen opens it at first) and onRequestIncrease is called when it opens; without a form the button only calls it, and without either there is no button. The limit, the terms and the next due date sit beside their words once the card is wide enough and under them in a narrow column. Due dates are <time> elements, every amount is in tabular figures, and currency, locale, timeZone, headingAs and labels do the usual.

items.name: trade-credit-summary-demo
items.title: Trade credit summary demo
items.description: A working preview of Trade credit summary.

items.name: warranty-registration
items.title: Warranty registration
items.description: Register a purchase for its warranty: serial number, purchase date and shop, proof of purchase, then the end date of the cover, shown before sending.
items.docs: Pass product ({ name, model?, image? }) when you know it: it is shown beside the form and the form does not ask for it; without it the form has a Product field. warrantyMonths (default 24) says how long the cover runs from the day of purchase. As soon as a day is chosen the form says 'Covered until 14 March 2028' before anything is sent, and a day in the future, or so old that the cover has already ended, is refused in words. serialPattern is a regular expression (a RegExp, or a string with its source, which can cross from a Server Component and is matched without regard to case): a serial number that does not fit is explained, with serialExample quoted ('It looks like HX-4821-K9Q2'; the same example is the empty field's placeholder, written 'For example HX-4821-K9Q2' so the field never looks filled in), and serialHelp says where the number is printed. The proof of purchase is one file up to maxFileSize bytes (default 5 MB) and is required unless proofRequired is false. onSubmit(values) receives { product, serial, purchaseDate (yyyy-mm-dd), store, proof (a File, or null), consent, coveredUntil (yyyy-mm-dd) }. Return a message and the form stays with every answer in it, the receipt's name too, and says so in a notice that takes focus; return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by the confirmation: the end of the cover as the one big fact, what was registered, what is covered (covers) and what is not (excludes). Return { reference } to print the registration's reference there, or pass submitted to show the confirmation for a registration your page already holds. defaultValues fills the shop and the day for a customer who comes from an order. now and timeZone decide which calendar day 'today' is (pass now from the server so the first render matches the browser's), locale writes the dates, privacyHref turns the consent line into a link, headingAs is 'h3' inside a section that has its own h2, and labels holds every fixed word for another language.

items.name: product-passport
items.title: Product passport
items.description: A digital product passport: what it is made of, where it was made, certifications, care and repair, and how to recycle it.
items.docs: Pass the parts you know and leave out the rest: a section without content is not drawn, never shown empty. materials ({ name, share in percent, note? }) draw one stacked bar with a list under it that writes every share in words, so the bar is never the only carrier of the numbers (the bar itself is hidden from screen readers); when the shares come to less than 100 the bar says 'Other materials' for the rest instead of claiming more than it knows. origin is { place, factory?, year?, note? }. certificates are { name, issuer?, number?, href }: each one is a real link to the certificate, opens in a new tab and says so to a screen reader. footprint is { value ('8.4 kg CO₂e'), label?, method? } with the method in one line. care, repair and endOfLife are lists of { title, detail?, icon?, href?, linkLabel? } in an accordion; defaultOpen says which of them start open (all three by default, [] for none). updatedAt is a Date, an ISO string or epoch milliseconds, and a plain yyyy-mm-dd is a calendar day; title and identifier name the product and the passport. locale writes the percentages and the date, timeZone reads updatedAt, headingAs is 'h3' inside a section that has its own h2 (the section titles, and the accordion's, go one level below it), and labels holds the fixed words. Apart from the accordion it keeps no state, so it renders on the server.

items.name: product-safety-info
items.title: Product safety information
items.description: The product safety facts regulations ask for: manufacturer and EU contact, model and batch, warnings, compliance marks and documents.
items.docs: Pass what you have: a section without content is left out, never shown empty. warnings are { severity ('danger' | 'warning' | 'caution' | 'notice'), title?, text }, most serious first. Every severity is written as a word ('Danger', 'Warning', 'Caution', 'Note') in front of the text, with an icon and a fill that grow stronger as the risk does, so nothing relies on colour or an icon alone. marks are { name ('CE'), description?, href? } and link to the declaration behind them. manufacturer and euContact are { name, address (an array of lines, or one string with line breaks), email?, phone?, website?, role? }, written in an address element with mail, call and web links. identifiers are { label, value, where? } for the model, the batch and the serial number and where each is printed. documents are { title, href, type?, size? (bytes), language? }, each with a download button that is only the icon in a narrow panel. updatedAt, locale and timeZone write 'Checked 12 October 2026' and the file sizes. linkAs renders the links with your router's Link, and action puts something at the right of the heading, such as the close button of a dialog, so nothing lies over the panel's own text, and stickyHeader pins that heading, and the button with it, to the top of whatever scrolls the panel, so the close button of a dialog never scrolls out of reach on a phone. The panel has no width of its own, so it sits as well in a tab or a dialog as on the page, and it keeps no state, so it renders on the server.

items.name: ranked-product-list
items.title: Ranked product list
items.description: Best sellers as a numbered list: a big rank figure, thumbnail, price, proof and a movement word, with a week, month or all-time switch.
items.docs: Pass items best first: a product's rank is its place in the array. An item is { id, name, href (the whole row is this link), price in minor units (8900 is 89.00), compareAtPrice?, subtitle?, image? ({ src, alt?, width?, height? }, drawn with renderImage so next/image plugs in), proof? (the line, already written: '1,240 sold this week'), rating?, ratingCount?, movement? and available? }. Movement is { kind: 'new' } | { kind: 'same' } | { kind: 'up' | 'down', by } and is always a word as well as an arrow ('New', 'Up 2', 'Down 1', 'Steady'): under the rank figure on a wide list, under the name on a phone. available false keeps the place but switches Add off and says 'Sold out'; a screen reader hears the product's name with 'is sold out' (soldOutName), so the words it sees are in the name it hears. The list is controlled: you hold period and pass the items for it. periods defaults to This week, This month and All time, and onPeriodChange is called with the value that was chosen (without it the periods are not offered and the list just names the one it shows). A polite status says which period the list shows and how many products. onAddToCart(item) may return a promise: the button shows it is working, says Added with a check and goes back to rest; when the promise rejects the button says Try again for a few seconds and a polite message tells a screen reader that the product could not be added; without it there are no buttons. The button is as wide as its longest word in every state, so the columns of the row never move when it changes. limit shows only the first places, linkAs renders the row links with your router's Link, currency and locale write the prices and numbers, and labels holds the fixed words. On a phone the picture shrinks, the proof moves under the name and the Add button is a square with the plus.

items.name: age-verification-gate
items.title: Age verification gate
items.description: A gate for age-restricted shops: what the shop sells, a date of birth or a plain over-18 choice, and a calm way out for those who fail.
items.docs: mode 'birthdate' (the default) asks for a date of birth in three number fields in the order of locale (day, month, year in most of the world, month first for en-US, year first for ja-JP) with the autofill hints a browser knows. It refuses dates that do not exist (31 February, month 13), a year that is not four digits and a day in the future, and puts focus on the field that is wrong. mode 'confirm' is two buttons: 'I am 18 or older' and 'I am under 18'. minimumAge defaults to 18. onVerify(birthdate, remember) is called when the visitor passes: birthdate is yyyy-mm-dd (undefined in confirm mode) and remember is the checkbox you get with rememberLabel; remembering the visitor, with a cookie or otherwise, is yours. A visitor who is too young gets a calm message and a way out, not an error and never a dead end: pass onDecline (the button 'Leave this site') or leaveHref (the same, as a link that works without a script), at least one of them, and in birthdate mode 'Typed the wrong date? Try again' goes back to the fields. presentation 'dialog' (the default) is a named modal that cannot be dismissed with Escape or a click outside, keeps focus inside, leaves nothing behind it reachable and gives focus back to what had it before it opened; without open it stays until the visitor passes, or pass open to control it. It is drawn in the browser, so the HTML from the server does not contain it and the shop behind it is reachable until the page has loaded: use presentation 'page' for a gate that has to be in the HTML. presentation 'page' renders the gate as a whole page (a section named by its heading, which is an h2, or an h1 with headingAs when the gate is the page), and nothing when open is false. title says what the shop sells ('This shop sells alcohol'); brand, note and helpHref ('Why do we ask?') add the rest. defaultDeclined starts on the message for a visitor who has answered already, now and timeZone decide what today is, autoFocus can be turned off when the gate is one of several things on a page, and labels holds the fixed words.

items.name: payment-plan-picker
items.title: Payment plan picker
items.description: Pay in full or in parts: plans as choice cards with the amount per payment, the total, and the schedule of the chosen plan beneath.
items.docs: total is the price of the order in minor units. plans are { id, payments, amount (one regular payment), total (everything the plan costs), apr?, firstPaymentToday?, label? }: a plan with one payment is 'Pay in full', what a plan costs above total is its interest, and a plan without any says 'No interest'. When total is not payments times amount the first payment takes the difference, so the schedule always adds up to the plan's total to the cent, and a line under the schedule says so in words ('The first payment is €205.45 because the cents do not divide evenly. The others are €205.41.'). The chosen plan's schedule is a real list beneath the cards: today, then one date a month in words (a plan that starts next month, firstPaymentToday false, has no 'today'; 31 January plus a month is 28 February), with the total, the interest and the representative APR under it. value, defaultValue and onValueChange control the choice, and onContinue(plan) adds a button. disclosure is whatever the law makes you say about this credit (a representative example, who provides it, what a missed payment means): it is always on the page under the plans, never behind a tooltip. now and timeZone give the calendar day the dates start from: pass now from the server so the first render already shows dates; without it the schedule says 'In 1 month' until the browser's clock is known and then turns those into dates. currency and locale write the amounts, a polite status says which plan was chosen, headingAs is 'h3' inside a section that has its own h2, and labels holds the fixed words.

items.name: price-transparency
items.title: Price transparency
items.description: Show where the money goes: a stacked bar of materials, making, shipping, duties and margin, with the typical retail price beside it.
items.docs: price is what the customer pays, in minor units; parts are { label, amount, note? } in minor units, in the order they are drawn. The bar is computed from the parts: a part with no money in it is left out, when the parts add up to less than the price the rest is drawn dashed as 'Other costs', and when they add up to more the price is what they add up to, so the bar always sums to the price; with no usable part at all the bar and the list are left out and the price stands alone, never as zero, and the comparison with the retail price still works. Every part is also a row with its amount and its share, the shares are whole percentages that add up to exactly 100, and the bar is hidden from screen readers because the list carries every number. A part's note opens from its name in a popover named after the part; hovering or focusing a row lights its part of the bar. retail is the typical retail price: with it the panel says how much lower this price is and shows both figures, without it there is nothing to compare. note is the small print under everything (what the figures are based on and when they were checked). currency and locale write the amounts and percentages, title and description name the product, headingAs is 'h3' inside a section that has its own h2, and labels holds the fixed words.

items.description: A working preview of Price transparency.

items.name: sample-request
items.title: Sample request
items.description: Order free samples before a big purchase: pick up to five swatches, see what is on its way, and add the delivery address in one short form.
items.docs: swatches are { id, name, color?, image?, note? }: a colour, a picture of the material (a URL or a data URI) or both, each a real checkbox with its name under it. limit (default 5) is the most samples one request can hold; at the limit the rest are switched off and the text beside the counter says why, while the chosen ones stay on so one can always be taken out. The counter ('Samples chosen: 3 of 5') is also the status region. value and onChange control the choice (the ids, in the order they were chosen), defaultValue starts it, and address fills the form for a customer who is signed in. Beside the grid sit the chosen samples, each with a button to take it out (focus moves to the next one), the delivery promise (deliveryNote: 'Free, arrives in 3 to 5 days') and the address. onSubmit({ swatchIds, address }) may return a promise. Return a message and the form stays with the samples and the address in it, and says so in a notice that takes focus; return nothing, or resolve, and the form is replaced by what is coming, where it is going and the order reference (return { reference } to print it). submitted shows that confirmation for a request your page already holds, shopHref adds the link back to the shop, locale writes the numbers, headingAs is 'h3' inside a section that has its own h2, and labels holds the fixed words.
